doc.title: Junior Mance Part II interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 18, 1999 [interview 2 of 2]

title: The trio with Earl May and Jackie Williams; Keter Betts and 'Blue Mance'
summary: How the Floating Jazz Festival trio began on a Benny Carter cruise and recorded 'Blue Mance'; the regular trio's playing.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Yeah, that was the day after the cruise. And so we recorded every time since then. But anyway, that’s why Keter, Keter lives in Washington, D.C. and he’s busy with a lot of things, and he’s on the Board I think of BET, the Black Entertainment Network in the jazz department. Like I see him playing on there so much you know with most of the groups, plus as I say he’s on the Board of Directors also. So he’s very busy. He’s involved in the Head Start program.
Right. Working with real little ones.

Right. Oh he loves doing that. So Earl May has been sort of our regular bass player. Earl is like a Rock of Gibraltar. He and Jackie like play so good together. And Jackie is like one of the best rhythm drummers I’ve played with. The two of them together. I heard a guy say once, “The time is so good you can set your watch by it.”
Well this tune also contains one of the best — I just have to play this lick.
Yeah but anyway, that night we just all felt good playing it, and it was a one take thing.
Yeah, I’ll have to send you the new one. It’s played the same but a different solo. And maybe something Jackie and Earl contributed to it. But Horst Weber, the producer, he loves that tune.
Well he’s got good taste then I think.
So we did it for him.
